bullets: Macro is mostly about not being on the wrong side of a regime change — positioning around structural shifts matters more than calling individual price moves.
Currency intervention is not always counter-productive; after 2023, selective intervention in thin overnight markets came to be seen as a legitimate tool rather than a reflexive mistake.
Risk you can articulate is risk you can manage — a pattern observed holding across three different teams, and one that makes downstream decisions easier once internalized.
Reliability of expectations is the underrated piece of macro analysis, with the second-order effect being the part most people miss.
Systems thinking applies because the dollar is a system, not a price; ignoring that means rebuilding the analysis from scratch a year later.
Trade-offs around systems thinking cut across risk management and macro policy, and framing matters because it reveals which trade-offs are actually being made.
Practical starting point: pick one idea and run it for two weeks rather than overhauling everything at once — the rest is iteration.
